expected.basis: No prior estimate possible — the page had zero affiliate links, so its C was structurally 0 and any traffic it earned converted at 0. This is a wiring fix, not a demand bet. First real expected-value scores start at iteration 2, once affiliate.byPage30d has data.

iterations.notes: Site's most-cited asset (CiteThisButton, Dataset JSON-LD, CC-licensed) had no route to a purchase — every outbound link was internal. Added InlineTextCta after the pricing tables and a compact CtaBanner after the economics section. Two placements not three: a reference page that reads as a sales pitch stops being cited. Page's lastUpdated is still 2026-04-08 — that is the Q3 study's job, not this one.

iterations.targetCluster: commercial lead-type queries (aged mortgage leads, aged insurance leads, final expense leads, iul leads)

expected.basis: 629 views/mo across the top four lead-type pages converting at ~0.95% today. Modelling C at 5% — 8x below the provider page's measured 43.33% — gives ~31 clicks vs 6, i.e. +25/mo on a 69-click base. A hypothesis to test, not a forecast: intent on a guide page is genuinely lower than on a provider review, and the gap will not fully close.

iterations.notes: Both hero buttons on these pages were internal (/compare, /price-index), so the site's highest-traffic commercial pages had no affiliate path above the fold. The mid-page CtaBanner also passes buttonHref, which sets useAffiliate=false — it is an internal compare link sitting exactly where intent peaks. Added a deep-linked door as the primary hero action; compare and pricing keep their position as secondary. Deep links verified per page: mortgage-leads -> /mortgage-leads-purchase-refinance/, final-expense-leads -> /life-insurance-leads/. insurance-leads correctly falls back to /all-lead-types/ — the partner has no generic-insurance buy page and that mapping is deliberate (lib/affiliate.ts, confirmed by Bill 2026-08-06). Destinations re-verified: 200, zero redirects, real buy pages ('Aged Mortgage Leads', 'Buy Aged Life Insurance Leads for Agents — From $0.25'). rel=nofollow sponsored and disclosure present on every instance. Measure via utm_content=hero-door.

iterations.asset: components/tracked-internal-link.tsx + hero compare door on providers/[slug]
iterations.targetCluster: competitor provider profiles (14 of 15) — merchant-evaluation intent

expected.basis: Deliberately unscored, and that is itself the finding. The scoreboard reports affiliate clicks per page (affiliate.byPage30d) but not pageviews for pages that produced zero affiliate clicks — so the 14 competitor profiles, which convert at 0 by construction, are invisible in it. Their D is unknown. What IS measured is the cost side: 61 of 130 outbound clicks in the 2026-08-18 reading left to competitor domains, against 69 affiliate clicks. This iteration does not forecast a number; it makes the 14 pages capable of producing one. Score it at the 2w read.

iterations.notes: LEAKAGE, not demand — a different failure mode from iterations 1 and 2. The site profiles 15 providers and monetizes 1. On the other 14 the only above-the-fold action was 'Visit Website', an unmonetized exit to a competitor (providers/[slug]/page.tsx:297). The monetized alternative already existed and was buried: all 14 aged-lead-store-vs-* head-to-heads are built and in the sitemap, but the only crawlable link to them sat in RelatedLinks at line 533 of a 559-line page, and the hero's other control (ProviderCompareSelector) is a <select> + router.push() that emits no <a href> and costs two interactions. Added a deep-linked compare door as the PRIMARY hero action on non-affiliate profiles; 'Visit Website' keeps its destination, rel and styling but becomes secondary. The competitor link is deliberately NOT removed — a review that will not link to its subject reads as captured, and editorial credibility is what makes these pages rank and convert. The affiliate profile's hero is untouched: there 'Visit Website' IS the money action (43.33% clickRate on 90 views, 39 of 69 affiliate clicks). Measurement is downstream, not on the button: this raises /compare/* pageviews and affiliate.byPage30d already attributes affiliate clicks per page, so the effect surfaces as compare-page affiliate clicks; the cta_click (compare-vs-als-<slug> @ provider-profile-hero) sizes the top of that funnel. Secondary benefit: 14 new crawlable, followed internal links into the best-converting format the site publishes, which previously had none.

scoreboardReadings.note: First reading from the per-page attribution built in iteration 0. Affiliate daily average of 2.30 is BELOW the 3/day flag threshold in CLICK-LOOP.md — but this counts GA4 outbound click events, while the 5.4/day baseline counts sessions arriving at agedleadstore.com. Different denominators; do not read one as a decline against the other. Trend this series against itself going forward.
